Aisha: Quick sync — we need to lock the calibration dataset and prompt bank for the INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ bakeoff. Key constraints: representative token distribution, no leakage from eval/test, include chat/instruction/code. What size and template strategy?
Ben: +1. My take — stratify by domain and token length. Suggested buckets: short (<32), medium (32-256), long (256-2048). Also split by task: classification/multiple-choice, instruction-following, open generation, code completion.
Diego: Add long-context streaming and multi-turn dialogue examples to the "long" bucket. Also include system prompts + role pairs so chat-mode quant errors surface.
Riley: For prompt templates, keep a small set of canonical templates and then 3 paraphrases each. Mix zero-shot and 1-shot templates. Avoid using golden outputs in calibration inputs (no labels in calib). Example templates: ```
T0: "Translate to French: {text}"
T1: "Write a short summary (3 sentences) for: {text}"
T2: "Given the following code, what does it do?
{code}"
```
Aisha: Good. Any strong opinions on calibration set size? I've seen people use 256-2048 examples — but AWQ/GPTQ sometimes ask for larger.
Ben: For INT8 activation calibration I'd aim for 2k representative examples (balanced across buckets). For AWQ/GPTQ per-layer stats, 3k-5k can reduce variance. So propose: default calib=2k, extended calib=5k for flaky patterns.
Diego: Emphasize token distribution > raw example count. 2k long docs != 2k short docs. Use stratified sampling by token-count to keep effective token coverage.
Riley: Also curate an "adversarial" small holdout (~200 examples) with common failure modes: math, nested lists, code edge-cases, instruction-ambiguity. Use that for quick sanity checks post-quant.
Aisha: How do we ensure no train/eval leakage? We should hash source IDs and block overlap, right?
Ben: Exactly. Use dataset fingerprints and a deterministic seed. Example command: `./scripts/build_calib.py --input data_manifest.json --out calib.json --size 2000 --stratify "len,domain" --seed 42`
Diego: Also run calibration collection with the same sampling temperature and tokenization as production. If production uses chat templates + few-shot, build those into calib samples.
Riley: For prompt bank curation, let's keep separate files: `calib_prompts.jsonl` (no labels), `eval_prompts.jsonl` (with labels), `adv_prompts.jsonl`. Version them in `eng-ml/evals/prompt-banks/` and tag commits with the bakeoff name.
Aisha: Nice. Any prefs for metric set for the bakeoff to compare quant variants?
Ben: Use a small battery: exact match / EM for closed QA, ROUGE-L for summarization, CodeBLEU for code, plus log-prob delta and calibration MAE (output distribution shift). Track per-bucket deltas.
Diego: And always report percentile latency and token-level perplexity delta. Some quant methods trade accuracy for latency too much.
Riley: I'll draft the prompt templates + stratified sampling script. Aisha — can you own gating the final calib vs eval split (and run overlap checks)?
Aisha: Yep I can. Plan: Riley builds drafts by EOD Thu, Ben runs a quick 2k calib + quant test Fri, Diego runs 5k extended runs on the AWQ nodes next week.
Aisha: Action items: Riley -> PR with templates and `build_calib` changes. Ben -> run baseline INT8 calib (2k). Diego -> schedule AWQ runs (5k). I'll verify no dataset overlap and push final samples to `eng-ml/evals/prompt-banks/`.
